summary: Koji Shindo is a scholar of Buddhist studies who was a graduate student at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (attested 2026). He served as a part-time lecturer at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 2015).

Koji Takahashi (1934–2023) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University (~1953–1957) and earned a doctorate from Bukkyo University (by 1991). He served at Bukkyo University as assistant professor (~1968–1980) and professor (~1980–2005).

Kojiro Yoshikawa (1904–1980) was a Sinologist who studied at Kyoto University (~1923–1926). He served as Professor of Chinese Language and Literature at Kyoto University (~1947–1967) and later as board chairman of Toho Gakkai (~1973–1980).

Kojun Fukui (1898–1991) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Waseda University under Sokichi Tsuda (~1921–1924, PhD 1949). He served as professor at Waseda (1941–1969) and as president of Taisho University (1972–1975).
Kojun Saito (1930–2002) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Seiren Matsunami. He served as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1965).
Kokan Fujita (1944–) is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Yujun Endo. He served as a professor at Koyasan University (attested 1995–2002).

Koken Sasaki (1931–2008) studied at Rissho University (~1950–1960) in Buddhist studies and Sinology. His career at Rissho University included roles as assistant professor (~1967–1975), chair of Buddhist studies (~1975–2002), and professor emeritus (~2002–2008).
Koki Kawagishi (1928–2011) was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at both Eizan Gakuin and Shitennoji University (both attested 1976).
Konchok Drakpa studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He also taught Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.
Konchok Gyatso is a Tibetology scholar who studied under Sherab Gyatso. He held a post at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2014).
Konchok Zangpo was a scholar who studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Konrad Klaus (1956–) is an Indology and Tibetology scholar who studied at Göttingen and Marburg (Promotion 1982–1985) under Michael Hahn. Between 1999 and 2001, he served as a substitute professor at Bochum, Marburg, and Bonn.

Kosaku Hamada (1881–1938) worked in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1901–1905), where he worked (~1909–1913) before holding a post at Kyoto University (~1913–1938).

Kosei Ishii (1950–) studied Buddhist studies and philosophy at Waseda University, completing a doctorate under Akira Hirakawa. He was an assistant professor at Komazawa Junior College (1994–2006) and a professor of Buddhism at Komazawa University (2006–2021).

Kosei Tada (1938–2017) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He served at Taisho University (~1970–2009) and as board chairman of the Society for Buddhist Cultural Studies (attested 2004).
Koshin Suzuki (1959–) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University. He served there as a researcher (attested 1995–1998).

Koshiro Tamaki (1915–1999) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, completing a doctorate at the University of Tokyo. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1964–1976), Tohoku University (~1976–1979), and Nihon University (1979–1986).

Kosho Kawamura (1924–) studied at Toyo University (~1948–1952) under mentors including Giyu Nishi and Koshiro Tamaki. He held research and teaching posts at Toyo University and became an honorary professor at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (attested 2001).

Kosho Mizutani (1928–2014) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku and Bukkyo universities (doctorate by 1979). He served Bukkyo University as assistant professor (~1961–1969) and president (~1979–1989), later chairing Bukkyo Kyoiku Gakuen (~1999–2011).

Kosho Uchiyama (1912–1998) studied Western philosophy at Waseda University (~1934–1937) and studied under Kodo Sawaki from 1941. In Buddhist studies and philosophy, he taught at Miyazaki Catholic Seminary (~1937–1939) and was abbot of Antai-ji (1965–1975).
